text:
maria: Heads-up — after the 1799910000 deploy we saw KV prefix cache hit-rate drop from ~92% -> ~58% during an autoscale spike. Noticed across eu-west pools.
kevin: Yikes. Any obvious eviction churn or memory pressure spikes?
jia: Can you paste the hotkey/eviction metrics?
maria: Pasted a quick snippet from prometheus: ```
kv_prefix_hit_rate{pool="eu-west-1"} 0.58  # avg over 5m
kv_prefix_hit_rate{pool="eu-west-1",job="preseeders"} 0.57
kv_evictions_total{pool="eu-west-1"} 4321  # last 10m
node_memory_used_bytes{node=~"gpu-.*"} 1.9e11
latency_p50_ms{route="generate"} 42 -> 95 (during spike)
```
sam: Also saw a short window where the prefill cron didn't run for ~7m (k8s job failed with RBAC error). Could explain reduced warm cache.
ops-bot: deploy event: service=runtime, version=2026.02.11-rc4, user=sam — started at 1799910105, finished 1799910132
maria: Sounds like a two-factor issue: (1) eviction threshold change we rolled in rc4, (2) scheduled prefill job didn't run.
kevin: Which eviction change? I remember an update to eviction heuristics to prefer LRU over size-aware for eager eviction.
jia: Right — PR #4267 changed kv.eviction.strategy=lruby (typo) -> lru and lowered kv.eviction.soft_limit from 120m -> 90m for high-concurrency pools. That would increase churn under load.
maria: Can confirm the running config on the affected node: ```
# from /etc/redwood/kv.conf
eviction.strategy = lru
eviction.soft_limit_mb = 90
eviction.max_entries = 200000
```
sam: If soft_limit lowered it will evict earlier and degrade hit-rate until warmers reseed. We also changed the key normalization for prompt prefixes in the same window (PR #4270) — could cause cache miss inflation (different key fingerprint).
kevin: Oof — keying + lower limits = double whammy. Any profiler captures?
maria: Captured a perf profile around the spike: top stack samples show heavy spending on serialize_key() and compare_key() with increased hash collisions.
kevin: That suggests the normalization change changed hash inputs. Jia, can you look at PR #4270?
jia: On it. Quick grep: we added trimming of whitespace and lowercasing, but accidentally kept original request id in the fingerprint for some routes. Bug: `fingerprint = fmt.Sprintf("%s|%s", prefix, r.RequestID)` — RequestID is unique -> guaranteed miss.
sam: That's the root cause for the missstorm. Good catch.
maria: Action plan proposed: 1) revert the keying change for the hot route (canary) 2) bump eviction.soft_limit back to 120m for eu-west pools 3) re-run the prefill job with higher parallelism and a conservative probe to rebuild KV heatmap 4) add a short-lived canary that seeds top 10k prefixes for 10m post-deploy.
kevin: I agree. Prioritize low-risk steps first: schedule prefill job, bump soft_limit, then revert keying if metrics don't recover.
ops-bot: k8s-job failed: prefill-job-eu-west-17999112 — reason: Forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:infra:prefill-sa" cannot create job.batch in namespace infra
maria: That's the RBAC blocker Sam spotted. Sam can you take infra on a quick RBAC fix?
sam: On it. I'll patch the SA binding and re-run prefill.
kevin: For the revert, we should do a canary on 2 nodes first. Use existing deploy rollback flow: `make rollback service=runtime version=2026.02.10`
maria: Also creating a lightweight prober so we can simulate the autoscale pattern without thrashing prod — helps validate warmers. Prober cmd: ```bash
# run against staging cluster
for p in $(cat top-prefixes.txt | head -n 5000); do 
  curl -sS -X POST $RUNTIME_URL/generate -d "{\"prefix\":\"$p\"}" >/dev/null &
done
wait
```
kevin: Good. Add a CI job that runs the prober and asserts hit-rate > 85% after prefill. We should gate merges that touch keying codepaths.
jia: I'll open PR to fix fingerprint generation and add tests that assert RequestID isn't included.
maria: I'm going to run the re-seed once RBAC is fixed and monitor `kv_prefix_hit_rate` and `kv_evictions_total` in real-time. I'll post a short update in 10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops-bot: job prefill-run-1799912345 started by sam at 1799912180
maria: Quick update: after bumping soft_limit and successful prefill run, hit-rate recovered to ~88% in 12m and latency p50 back to ~46ms. Not fully back to baseline but much better.
kevin: Nice. Next steps: long-term, add canary for keying changes + unit tests for fingerprinting + a scheduled weekly small prefill to keep tails warm.
sam: I've fixed the RBAC and re-run the prefill. Logs show ~9.2k prefixes seeded.
jia: PR #4283 opened to strip RequestID from fingerprint and add regression tests.
maria: Thanks all. I'll leave a short postmortem note with the timeline and action items. If anyone sees residual skew, ping me. :thumbsup:
kevin: Great convo — good catch on the RequestID insertion.:+1:
